note.text:
To interpret data, look for a pattern, often on a graph.
• The quantity we change goes along the bottom (x-axis); the quantity we measure goes up the side (y-axis).
• Read a value: go up from the x value to the line, then across to the y-axis.
• The trend: as x increases, y increases, decreases or stays the same. A straight line through 0 means y is proportional to x: double x, double y.
• The rate of increase is how much y goes up for each 1 unit of x.
A conclusion answers the question of the experiment using the data: “As the time increases, the distance increases steadily.” It must not claim more than the data show.

worked_example.problem: A trolley's distance is measured every second: {readings([0, k, 2 * k, 3 * k, 4 * k])} m at the times {readings([0, 1, 2, 3, 4])} s. Describe the trend and find the distance at {x} s.
steps: Each second the distance increases by the same amount, {k} m: the trend is a steady increase.
At {x} s the distance is {x} × {k} = {x * k} m.
worked_example.answer: Steady increase of {k} m each second; {x * k} m at {x} s.

cards.idea: To read a graph, go up from the x value to the line, then across to the y-axis.
example: At {x} s, go up to the line and across: {x * k} m.

cards.idea: The trend tells what happens to y as x increases: it increases, decreases or stays the same.
example: A line going up from left to right: y increases.
A line going down: y decreases.

cards.idea: A conclusion uses the data to answer the question, without claiming more than the data show.
example: Good: “As the mass increases, the stretch increases.”
Too much: “Every spring in the world stretches the same.”

questions.prompt: The graph shows the distance travelled by a trolley. What distance has it travelled after {x} s?

misconceptions.explain: {x} is the time; read the distance on the side axis.

solution: Go up from {x} s to the line, then across to the distance axis.
questions.figure: lineGraph(xs, [0, k, 2 * k, 3 * k, 4 * k, 5 * k], 'time (s)', 'distance (m)')

pick: The longer a pot of water is heated, the higher its temperature.
The temperature goes up as time goes on.
The further a torch is from a wall, the dimmer the light on the wall.
The light gets dimmer as the distance grows.
The more mass hung on a spring, the longer the spring.
The spring gets longer as the mass grows.
As a hot drink cools in a room, its temperature falls.
The temperature goes down as time goes on.

questions.prompt: From the graph, by how many metres does the distance increase each second?

misconceptions.explain: That is the total after five seconds; the increase each second is {k} m.

solution: Read two points: at {one} s the distance is {k} m, at {two} s it is {2 * k} m.
The increase each second is {2 * k} − {k} = {answer} m.
questions.figure: lineGraph(xs, [0, k, 2 * k, 3 * k, 4 * k, 5 * k], 'time (s)', 'distance (m)')

questions.prompt: A pupil heated water and recorded that its temperature rose by the same amount every minute. Which conclusion is best?

right.text: As the heating time increases, the temperature of the water increases steadily.
The temperature of the water rose at a steady rate while it was heated.

wrong.explain: The data do not show that.

wrong.text: All liquids heat up at the same rate as water.
wrong.explain: Only water was tested: the data cannot say that.

wrong.text: The temperature went down while heating.
wrong.explain: The data show it went up.
That does not answer the question from the data.

questions.prompt: Distance is proportional to time in this experiment: in {t} s the trolley goes {t * k} m. How far does it go in {2 * t} s?

misconceptions.explain: Proportional means multiply: double the time gives double the distance.

solution: Proportional: double the time, double the distance.
